GRUDGELANDS / ROUND 70 / LAND USE STUDY

Room for a crown.
Room to arrive.

Six capital cores. Six start towns. One shared castle reservation, twelve places with their own character.

2D proposal · GPT-6 Astra07 November 2026Base 55aa7708

Reserve the land.
Decide the buildings later.

The recommendation is a 45 × 35-node castle reservation, turned to suit each capital, inside a civic core expanded by eight nodes per side. Lethariel keeps the castle on its dry western shoulder; Kezamba keeps it on the dry southern terrace.

At the starts, give each waystone a clear 13 × 13 pocket near the centre. Move the closest buildings and furniture to make space, while keeping the town envelope, spawn and gate axis.

Proposal, not an approved build

No castle architecture is designed here. Gold shapes reserve land, including future overhangs. Existing buildings and sockets come from the real template/composition code.

An independent check confirmed the layouts and cost claims against the code. Desktop and web walking, final heights, future 3D geometry and combat remain unverified.

Shared footprint: 1,575 square nodes. Hall-floor reservation: 35 × 23 = 805 within it. Two royal posts beside the throne and two ordinary door guards at the great door. No extra guards.

Reading the plans

North (+z) is up; +x is right. All twelve plan pairs use the same 160-node window and a 20-node scale bar. Solid blocks are exported template pivots; faint outlines include eaves and other written columns. Numbers match the coordinate schedules. Q marks a quest giver, V a vendor, O the public oven. Click or focus a numbered building to highlight it in both views.

Today’s background is a schematic projection of actual authored cells, with trees and paving. The proposed background keeps surrounding planting schematically and shows land reservations and principal walking connections; it is not a new voxel blueprint. Existing lake samples are from seed 12345; all three seeds were checked beneath the castle reservations.

THE TWO DECISIONS

A larger hall. Space around it.

The shared castle stays 45×35 = 1,575 nodes². The former proposal reserved only 23×15 = 345 for its throne room. The new hall-floor reservation is 35×23 = 805 in every castle. Today’s gross hall in five capitals is 29×25 = 725: the new reservation adds 80 nodes² (about 11%), while depth shrinks from 25 to 23. The checker measured today’s reachable floor as 684 in those five capitals and 402 in Kezamba. Comparing 805 with those net areas gives +121 (+17.7%) and +403 (+100.2%); these compare new gross with old net floor, not measured gains in reachable space. The new hall’s walls are outside its reservation: 304 nodes² for the two-node outer wall band, 120 for the one-node hall wall ring, and 346 for foyer, stairs, service space and circulation. Together they use exactly 1,575. This is a compact hall-led castle; no separate ground-level courtyard is promised. The later architecture must keep this room reservation and provide more reachable floor than today after placing the throne and furnishings; 805 is the reserved floor area, not a measured furnished result. The 96×96 rule needs coordinated documentation changes in settlements.md and world_zones.md:721/810/1741/1765 (also the 96-node wording at 1865). Duplicated composition coordinates need updating too: for example Sunscar’s BREASTWORKS still names the original hall and armoury boxes separately from their layout placements. C089

48 or 56: what the extra land buys

The Dur Brannoc, Highcourt, Gor Drazhak and Nhal Veyr castle boxes already fit inside today’s ±49. Only these four capitals have an optional growth choice as drawn. Lethariel and Kezamba need growth as placed: with the five-node avenues kept, a quadrant ending at ±46 offers only 44 nodes (3…46), shorter than the castle’s 45-node side. Staying at 48 there would require straddling an axis or hugging the ring; neither is proposed here. For the four compact alternatives, 48’s main saving is dropping most of C003 for cores kept at that radius: gatehouse relocation, ring-street and boundary expansion, changes to RADIUS, civic_width and BOUNDS, the larger collar, moved landing scan and city_green expansion. It also avoids their radius-induced district land loss. Shared machinery still needs changes if any core grows; castle, socket and furniture work remains. The compact castle moves six nodes south to (−22,4)…(22,38), keeps the old gatehouses, narrows the approach 9→5 and bypass 5→3, and leaves only z=3 between crossing and great door. Today’s great-door ascent uses two stair rows at z=7 and 8; the one compact row is already Dur Brannoc’s kerb, so stairs must enter the foyer. In all four capitals the north gate’s watch rectangle (x=−4…4, z=37…41) overlaps the castle and bypass and needs rerouting. Eastern work buildings move six nodes (Highcourt’s yard also one north); Highcourt moves its chapel west and retires north_house and chapel_house. Markets and colonnades keep their present spacing. These alternatives pass footprint, street-width and door-exit checks only; their stairs and watch routes remain unresolved and they need their own socket/furniture schedules. Both radius choices join Round 70’s already required map reset. Changed rivers cost one full seed-fleet run within that work, with no additional reset. Rivers stay unchanged by civic growth only if all six capitals stay at 48. The 40-seed table measures all six at 56; a mixed 48/56 choice is unmeasured. Keeping 48 departs from §2.7’s ruling that the civic core grows somewhat; the user may still choose it. Recommendation: 56 for moved neighbours, the forecourt and bypass, accepting the coordinated implementation work above. C091

Same scale as the twelve main plan pairs. These are land alternatives, without socket or furniture layouts. Building numbers match each capital’s main key. The recommended 56 layouts appear below.

40 fleet seeds · all six at 56, with today’s cores

The checker measured 40 fleet seeds with all six capitals at radius 56: civic_width=112 and CORE/CORE_GATE/CORE_KEEP=56/57/60, using today’s authored cores and landing detector. A mixed 48/56 choice is unmeasured; this table does not predict it. All 240 proposed capitals placed every required plot, with no load failure; castle samples were dry and flat. Seven capital/seed unrouted-street cases appeared and three disappeared. Infeasible seeds: Kezamba 3→3, Lethariel 0→2, Gor Drazhak 2→0; the others 0→0. This differs from the three-seed MASK-ONLY experiment, which retains civic_width=96. On seed 12345 the proposed plot totals are Dur Brannoc 50 (mask only) versus 47 (civic112), and Kezamba 49 versus 51. Neither experiment builds the new cores. The implementation must run tools/seed_fleet/run.sh full, not just these 40 seeds, because civic_width changes terrain and river planning for every seed. C090

BEFORE A BUILD

The dependencies behind the lines

Verified encounter rules

Two royal guards are deliberate. Both door guards are ordinary guards. The four-guard documentation is stale. The 60-node distance concerns rewards; the king’s 30-node leash starts where a chase began and cannot confine combat to this room.

Read the 14 shared dependencies and evidence links
  • The enlarged core consumes district land: CORE/CORE_GATE/CORE_KEEP change from 48/49/52 to 56/57/60. The buildable mask also excludes wet, bank-adjacent and rough samples. The nominal civic square gains 3,328 square nodes (+36.1%); the outer 512-node reservation is unchanged. C001
  • This is a planner sensitivity experiment: real world assembly and capital planning, with only those three options enlarged. Existing civic_width=96, terrain, buildings and the old core_landing detector remain. Final earthwork, landing heights, collision-free generated streets and performance are not verified. C002
  • Implementation of radius 56 must coordinate civic_width 96→112; CORE/CORE_GATE/CORE_KEEP 48/49/52→56/57/60; RADIUS=49 in all six Lua compositions; precinct_ring.RADIUS=48; the ±47 corner towers in Dur Brannoc, Gor Drazhak and Nhal Veyr; city_green.CORE_HALF=49; the flat-core/collar and road fitting; BOUNDS.capital_core ±49→±57 and the separate ±49 plot-collar exclusion; r7_capitals core_landing 46…49 and built=96*96. The river keep-out formula grows from 99.9 to 111.2 nodes and can change rivers world-wide. Both radius choices already join Round 70’s map reset; the river consequence needs one full seed-fleet run within that work, with no additional reset. Rivers stay unchanged by civic growth only if all six capitals stay at 48. The outer capital reservation stays 512 nodes. C003
  • All six cities have four planned OUTER gates. Core entries differ: four authored gatehouses in Dur Brannoc, Highcourt, Gor Drazhak and Nhal Veyr; three in Lethariel; no such gatehouse kit in Kezamba. Extend the dry core entries by eight nodes, rebuild boundary rings and connect each avenue; do not add a northern gatehouse across Lethariel’s lake. C004
  • The avenue starts at CORE_GATE+1; when its core landing is wet it searches for a dry shore start. core_landing still scans along 46…49 and y −1…1. New dry thresholds and Kezamba’s deck extensions need a corresponding landing scan and height check; the lake edge must not silently acquire a land bridge. C005
  • Patrol routes cache each fixed leg by settlement and body class in memory. Longer capital patrol legs may follow generated streets (street reach 24, rise 6); failed legs can remain unavailable until restart. Re-author waypoint groups/order and test doors, stairs and clear walking corridors; there is no saved route-cache migration to design. C006
  • Exactly two royal guards is deliberate, since commit 494a6073: only throne_guard_west/east bind to the king. door_guard_west/east remain ordinary guard posts at the great door; all four positions are shown. There are no unbound spare guards. Later documentation cleanup must correct world.md:497–498, world_zones.md:1869/1876/1886–1888/1898, biomes_mobs.md:849 and the comment in start_npcs.lua:921. These stale four-guard and five-NPC statements do not authorize changing the encounter. C007
  • The 60-node rule is a 3D reward-participation distance to the king’s death position (with a separate 60-second death grace). king_def instead sets a 30-node chase leash; aggro measures it from the chase anchor. Royal guards have no independent leash and use a 5-node follow distance. The new room is an 805-node² floor reservation, not a combat boundary: the king can chase out of it and the chase anchor can move between pulls. No existing mechanism keeps combat in the room; this proposal changes neither leash nor encounter rules. C008
  • Required capital plots are the eight service plots, the inn and miners_guild. Moving a plot moves its rotated sockets with it; ids keep the plot_id/socket_id prefix. The service annexes list the concrete bindings to preserve, including guild leader/exchange/clerk/sorter/porter, innkeeper, Housing Steward, Crownbinder and Decor Merchant. C009
  • Start towns keep the same 128-node fitting/protection pad, rounded 12-node protected band and authored ±63 building limits. The proposed centres use existing town land; spawn stays at (0,1,0), and the main_street gate axis stays. Foundations, stairs, doorsteps, vegetation and ground patterns displaced by the moves must be re-authored inside that envelope. C010
  • Each proposed start waystone keeps the reach-3 pad, inside a new 13×13 clear arrival reservation. Move travel_waypoint, the stone, its paving and mailbox together. Mail is at (+2,+1) from the stone; arrival tries the authored side or +x first, then the other sides. Keep all four neighbouring standing cells and the lane connection open. C011
  • Quest identities bind to settlement/socket, and registry validation requires role=quest. Every start has both hall_quest and the projection adapter’s quest_cook/cook_oven; the latter are at (2,±13)/(4,±13), not in the town .layout. Preserve them, the Quartermaster id, home socket and spare standing spots when re-authoring the centre. C012
  • Socket y, facing and free feet/head/floor must be checked on the final built geometry. The runtime tries the socket and up to two cells above it before postponing placement; a 2D reservation does not prove standing or walking clearance. No Luanti server or desktop/web runtime was run here. C013
  • This lane is tools-only and changes no world state. Building the selected cores or towns changes map generation and belongs to Round 70’s map reset. No migration step, online rewrite or production deployment is supplied by this design. C014
01 / CAPITAL · The Accord

Dur Brannoc

A citadel above the forge court

A broad castle closes the northern view. The working court shifts east; the ancestor hall keeps its quiet western edge.

Granite court · slate halls · western ancestor precinct

31×27 → 45×35royal footprint · 837 → 1,575 nodes²+8 nodes / sidenominal civic radius 48 → 5635×23 = 805hall-floor reservation · walls separate

Today’s gross hall: 29 × 25 = 725 nodes² → 35 × 23 = 805 (+80, about 11%); depth shrinks from 25 to 23. Against the checker’s 684 reachable nodes², the 17.7% compares new gross with old net floor, not a measured gain in reachable space. The former 345-node² reservation is replaced. Walls, foyer and service circulation have separate budgets above.

The castle nearly doubles the old hall’s land reservation while the forge remains visible from the central crossing. Two flank lanes carry through traffic behind the castle.

The western market shifts five nodes outward, its edge house shifts seven, and the statue moves three nodes east so the wider colonnades have room.

31×27 → 45×35royal footprint · 837 → 1,575 nodes²+8 nodes / sidenominal civic radius 48 → 5635×23 = 805hall-floor reservation · walls separate

Today’s gross hall: 29 × 25 = 725 nodes² → 35 × 23 = 805 (+80, about 11%); depth shrinks from 25 to 23. The western market shifts five nodes outward, its edge house shifts seven, and the statue moves three nodes east so the wider colonnades have room.

What this commits the implementation to

  • Lethariel: reserve the shared castle at (-52, -51)–(-18, -7), facing east. Relocate 3 core templates; retire colonnade_west, colonnade_east as freestanding strips; the full export also contains 60 Lua-authored or generated sockets outside template ownership, among 98 exported points, in a 945-line composition. Those points, their furniture and duplicate coordinates all need review; this is not merely a template translation. The schedule includes every exported socket. Template envelopes, door exits, full road widths and socket collisions against exported template cells are checked; final 3D routes remain unverified. C029
  • Lethariel: move the three inner gatehouses and the open lake shore with the expanded boundary. The four outer gates and their avenues are replanned per seed; their measured positions are in the city views. Update core_landing, boundary masking and the road/collar exclusions together. C030
  • Lethariel: re-author watch_south_west, watch_west, watch_quay, watch_south_east in lethariel_watch; the proposed points are in the socket schedule. Keep Lethariel’s quay patrol dry and regenerate the three gate watches. Rebuild the in-memory route legs after restart and test them on the finished geometry. C031
  • Lethariel: king moves from (-38, -25) to (-46, -29); throne_guard_west/east follow to posts three nodes away. Preserve their ids and royal binding, then author their y and facing from the actual throne floor. The 60-node reward sphere follows the death position; it is not a core boundary. Keep door_guard_west/east as ordinary guards at the great door, and carry hall_idle_west/east/service and hall_waypoint into the new floor allocation; add no guard slots. C032
  • Lethariel: preserve star_hall_quest at its named public building and keep vendor_race/vendor_general at their unchanged positions. travel_waypoint is proposed at (25, -14); keep its mailbox and arrival cells with it. All ten required district plots and the concrete service sockets listed below must survive replanning; no service is transferred to the castle. C033
  • Lethariel: preserve the MERE wedge and its one-node shore margin, including the tip at (0,22); enlarge on the dry south-west. The mere district remains pinned toward lethariel_crown_lake. Extend the authored mask from the water source if the core boundary changes; do not extrapolate the present finite MERE table blindly. C034

Those points, their furniture and duplicate coordinates all need review; this is not merely a template translation. The schedule includes every exported socket. Template envelopes, door exits, full road widths and socket collisions against exported template cells are checked; final 3D routes remain unverified. C036

  • Gor Drazhak: re-author watch_south_west, watch_north_west, watch_north_east, watch_south_east in gor_drazhak_watch; the proposed points are in the socket schedule. Regenerate each moved gate_watch rectangle and tower post from its stamped gate. Rebuild the in-memory route legs after restart and test them on the finished geometry. C038

Preserve their ids and royal binding, then author their y and facing from the actual throne floor. The 60-node reward sphere follows the death position; it is not a core boundary. Keep door_guard_west/east as ordinary guards at the great door, and carry hall_idle_west/east/service and hall_waypoint into the new floor allocation; add no guard slots. C039

All ten required district plots and the concrete service sockets listed below must survive replanning; no service is transferred to the castle. C040
  • Gor Drazhak: carry the larger core onto the fitted civic ground, keeping its own boundary character. civic_width, authorized core bounds and road/plot-collar exclusions must change together; the three-seed comparison does not include this earthwork. C041

05 / CAPITAL · The Throng

Nhal Veyr

A sovereign precinct in the necropolis

The small mausoleum gives way to the shared castle reservation. A rear processional walk separates the royal precinct from the northern gate.

Funerary court · iron boundary · western vigil hall

31×27 → 45×35royal footprint · 837 → 1,575 nodes²+8 nodes / sidenominal civic radius 48 → 5635×23 = 805hall-floor reservation · walls separate

Today’s gross hall: 29 × 25 = 725 nodes² → 35 × 23 = 805 (+80, about 11%); depth shrinks from 25 to 23. Against the checker’s 684 reachable nodes², the 17.7% compares new gross with old net floor, not a measured gain in reachable space. The former 345-node² reservation is replaced. Walls, foyer and service circulation have separate budgets above.

Bone Works and the Charnel Yard move east. The existing close patrol around the mausoleum must be replaced by a loop around the enlarged precinct.

The western market shifts five nodes outward, its edge house shifts seven, and the statue moves three nodes east so the wider colonnades have room.

C008 · Read + proposed consequence

The 60-node rule is a 3D reward-participation distance to the king’s death position (with a separate 60-second death grace). king_def instead sets a 30-node chase leash; aggro measures it from the chase anchor. Royal guards have no independent leash and use a 5-node follow distance. The new room is an 805-node² floor reservation, not a combat boundary: the king can chase out of it and the chase anchor can move between pulls. No existing mechanism keeps combat in the room; this proposal changes neither leash nor encounter rules.

C087 · Proposal / gross dimensions checked, reported net measurement

The shared castle stays 45×35 = 1,575 nodes². The former proposal reserved only 23×15 = 345 for its throne room. The new hall-floor reservation is 35×23 = 805 in every castle. Today’s gross hall in five capitals is 29×25 = 725: the new reservation adds 80 nodes² (about 11%), while depth shrinks from 25 to 23. The checker measured today’s reachable floor as 684 in those five capitals and 402 in Kezamba. Comparing 805 with those net areas gives +121 (+17.7%) and +403 (+100.2%); these compare new gross with old net floor, not measured gains in reachable space. The new hall’s walls are outside its reservation: 304 nodes² for the two-node outer wall band, 120 for the one-node hall wall ring, and 346 for foyer, stairs, service space and circulation. Together they use exactly 1,575. This is a compact hall-led castle; no separate ground-level courtyard is promised. The later architecture must keep this room reservation and provide more reachable floor than today after placing the throne and furnishings; 805 is the reserved floor area, not a measured furnished result.

C090 · Measured by checker / aggregates rechecked, today’s cores

The checker measured 40 fleet seeds with all six capitals at radius 56: civic_width=112 and CORE/CORE_GATE/CORE_KEEP=56/57/60, using today’s authored cores and landing detector. A mixed 48/56 choice is unmeasured; this table does not predict it. All 240 proposed capitals placed every required plot, with no load failure; castle samples were dry and flat. Seven capital/seed unrouted-street cases appeared and three disappeared. Infeasible seeds: Kezamba 3→3, Lethariel 0→2, Gor Drazhak 2→0; the others 0→0. This differs from the three-seed MASK-ONLY experiment, which retains civic_width=96. On seed 12345 the proposed plot totals are Dur Brannoc 50 (mask only) versus 47 (civic112), and Kezamba 49 versus 51. Neither experiment builds the new cores. The implementation must run tools/seed_fleet/run.sh full, not just these 40 seeds, because civic_width changes terrain and river planning for every seed.

C091 · Alternative / bounded 2D checked, stairs and watch routes unresolved

The Dur Brannoc, Highcourt, Gor Drazhak and Nhal Veyr castle boxes already fit inside today’s ±49. Only these four capitals have an optional growth choice as drawn. Lethariel and Kezamba need growth as placed: with the five-node avenues kept, a quadrant ending at ±46 offers only 44 nodes (3…46), shorter than the castle’s 45-node side. Staying at 48 there would require straddling an axis or hugging the ring; neither is proposed here. For the four compact alternatives, 48’s main saving is dropping most of C003 for cores kept at that radius: gatehouse relocation, ring-street and boundary expansion, changes to RADIUS, civic_width and BOUNDS, the larger collar, moved landing scan and city_green expansion. It also avoids their radius-induced district land loss. Shared machinery still needs changes if any core grows; castle, socket and furniture work remains. The compact castle moves six nodes south to (−22,4)…(22,38), keeps the old gatehouses, narrows the approach 9→5 and bypass 5→3, and leaves only z=3 between crossing and great door. Today’s great-door ascent uses two stair rows at z=7 and 8; the one compact row is already Dur Brannoc’s kerb, so stairs must enter the foyer. In all four capitals the north gate’s watch rectangle (x=−4…4, z=37…41) overlaps the castle and bypass and needs rerouting. Eastern work buildings move six nodes (Highcourt’s yard also one north); Highcourt moves its chapel west and retires north_house and chapel_house. Markets and colonnades keep their present spacing. These alternatives pass footprint, street-width and door-exit checks only; their stairs and watch routes remain unresolved and they need their own socket/furniture schedules. Both radius choices join Round 70’s already required map reset. Changed rivers cost one full seed-fleet run within that work, with no additional reset. Rivers stay unchanged by civic growth only if all six capitals stay at 48. The 40-seed table measures all six at 56; a mixed 48/56 choice is unmeasured. Keeping 48 departs from §2.7’s ruling that the civic core grows somewhat; the user may still choose it. Recommendation: 56 for moved neighbours, the forecourt and bypass, accepting the coordinated implementation work above.
